A copper disk is installed on a vertical copper axle, and two copper sheets P and Q respectively contact the edge of the disk and the copper axle. The disk is in a uniform magnetic field B directed vertically upward. When the disk rotates, regarding the current flowing through resistor R, which of the following statements is correct? (　　)

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: The schematic diagram of a Faraday disk generator is shown in Figure 11. A copper disk is installed on a vertical copper axle, and two copper sheets P and Q respectively contact the edge of the disk and the copper axle. The disk is in a uniform magnetic field B directed vertically upward. If the angular velocity of the disk's rotation is constant, how does the magnitude of the current flowing through resistor R change?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: the figure is a schematic diagram of a Faraday disk generator: a horizontal copper disk is installed on a vertical copper axle, with copper sheet P in contact at the edge of the disk and copper sheet Q in contact at the copper axle; P and Q are connected to resistor R through an external circuit, and a and b are marked on the left side; in the disk region there are multiple vertically upward arrows labeled B, indicating that the uniform magnetic field is vertically upward, and a rotation direction arrow is also drawn on the disk. Reasoning: according to the problem statement, regard the disk as countless conducting radii from the axis center to the edge. What the external circuit actually takes is the potential difference between the axle Q and the edge P. When the disk rotates with constant angular velocity ω, the magnitude of the linear velocity at a distance r from the axis center is v=ωr; the magnetic field B is uniform and constant, so the motional electromotive force along the radial direction is ε=∫(v×B)·dl, with magnitude ∫_0^L Bωr dr=1/2·BωL^2, where L is the radius of the disk. Since B, ω, and L all remain unchanged, the magnitude of the electromotive force is constant; when the resistance of the external circuit remains unchanged, the magnitude of the current flowing through resistor R is also constant. Final answer: the current magnitude is constant.
